`compute_rep_stats` returns a 4-tuple whose fourth element is the fraction spread. `barplot/collect.py:429` binds it as `g_err_f`; these three siblings discard it (`, _ =`) and then hard-set `gfe = 0.0`. The Line tab's Fraction panel and the batch bar path lose their error band entirely while the Bar tab keeps it.
`LinePoint.n_above_spread` is populated at `:335` and then ignored at the draw site, which passes a literal `0.0`. The Line tab's Events panel never shows a replicate error bar the Bar tab does show.

The FOV branch of `group_replicate_stats` never consults `fov_integrity.check_fov_labels`, the verdict that exists because "six fields pooled under one label turn the mean events per field into the total — six times too large". An untrustworthy well reads "undefined" as a solo bar and 6× as a set member, in one figure.
The gate percentage is denominated by the already gate-filtered cloud, so "Apply gates" makes every label read `100.0%`.
`_sync_err_from_app` never writes `bar_err_kind`, so `ci95` survives a SEM/SD flip: bars draw 1.96 × SD under a label reading "SD".

The stats-cache keys fold in `active_val_col` — a bare `ratio:<name>` string — but never `ratio_index`, and `channel_state_controller.set_ratio_metrics:831` never calls `invalidate_stats_cache` (twelve other mutation sites do). Editing a ratio in place leaves every rep-set entry valid by key and wrong by value.
The replicate-set average is a pool-of-cells mean, not the mean-of-per-well-means Bar, Line and Stats use. Possibly deliberate; undocumented either way.
The optimizer's fraction-on population (QC + Crop only) is not the plots' denominator, so its reported fractions and its argmax do not match the bar plot.
`has_frac` couples to `has_mean` only in the grouped branch: a set with zero above-threshold cells shows a placeholder pooled and an honest 0 unpooled.
The per-cell Events panel ignores `bar_err_settings`, so "None" and "95 % CI" apply to grouped mode only.
`x_by_key` collapses duplicate keys in multi-timepoint mode, so significance brackets are drawn over the last timepoint's bars rather than the tested one.
`_num(...) or None` drops a deliberately typed `0` bound.
`isinstance(x, (int, float))` rejects `numpy.float32`, giving a NaN mean and a lost error bar. Latent (no live float32 producer found) but the exact class CLAUDE.md §7.5 #8 records in this module.
The line CSV writes a literal `nan` spread where the bar CSV writes `""`.
Docstring says epsilon is *added*; the resolver *clamps* (`np.maximum(den, epsilon)`) — different numbers near and below zero on background-subtracted channels.

Every baseline search requires `v != 0`, so a fraction-on or event count of exactly 0 at t0 — the expected value of an induction experiment — is skipped and a **later timepoint** is silently substituted. Measured: the mean panel normalizes to t=0 while the fraction and events panels normalize to t=24, in one figure under one axis label. For *ratio* mode skipping a zero divisor is defensible; for *subtract* mode subtracting 0 is well-defined and the skip is simply wrong.
`ax_frac.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)` unconditionally, so under fold change the fraction panel clips every ratio above 1.05 out of view. Bar's `_set_frac_ylim` skips the clamp for exactly this reason.
The violin/beeswarm Fraction panel plots raw fractions but is given the fold-change title suffix. `draw_per_well_n_bars` guards against this; the fraction panel does not.

`PlotState`'s fold-change block (`fc_vs_control_on`, `fc_control`, `fc_control_map`, `focus_timepoint`, `line_order_*`, `bar_group_mode`) is never reset on a dataset swap, and `view_state.load_from_data_dir` early-returns when the new plate has no saved block. Plate B comes up normalized against plate A's group — every bar NaN under a fold-change axis label.
The line path folds an undefined (NaN) spread to `0.0`; the bar path preserves NaN. `scale_bar_value`'s own docstring states the rule `_scale_pt` breaks four hundred lines above it.
An inherited per-member control mode shows `—` in the Control combo while the export normalizes anyway.
The events replicate spread (index 9) is not normalized while its value (index 4) is. Invisible only because the Line draw site passes `0.0` for that panel.

`tick_labels` de-duplicates by reference and `distinct_controls` by resolved wells, so a one-well control set plus that well's own token gives an axis title naming one control above tick rows naming two.
One row edit rebuilds the table twice, and `setCellWidget` destroys the combo whose slot is still on the stack — roughly 192 combos per edit on a 96-member plate.
A bare `except → frozenset()` with no log makes `redraw_scopes_or_defer` defer every scope: the fold-change controls silently stop working.

Both classifiers call `Path(stripped).stem` on an **already-stripped field stem**, truncating any schema token that contains a dot. Reproduced: `classify_filename_role("A1_f1_1.5h_w2_labels.tif")` → `(MASK, 'A1_f1_1')`. A `1.5h` mask or tophat is keyed `tp="1"`, so it loses its own mask *and* collides with the genuine `1h`/`T01` key on a first-hit-wins lookup.
The loose-file fallback's `else:` files `smfish` images into the **mask** dict; `load_mask_array` then `rint`s spot intensities into an int32 label image.
The ambiguity refusal covers an empty FOV but not an empty timepoint, which matches every key and returns `hits[0]` as a successful `"normalized"` resolution.

The wrap-cols banded layout derives its single column-header strip from row 0 only, so every band below the first is labelled with the *first* band's values (2 ch × 6 tp, wrap 3 → rows 2–3 show T4–T6 under a header reading T1–T3). Export replays the same plan. Documented as a known limitation at ARCHITECTURE line 2141; nothing in the UI says so.
Row labels read only column 0 and column labels only row 0, so a deliberately blank cell there deletes that band's axis label instead of falling back to a populated cell.

`normalize_numeric_token` uses `str(value or "")`, so numeric zero becomes `""` — dropping a `0` entry from `timepoint_options`/`fov_options` and turning an empty target into "match anything". `image_identity._raw_token` documents this exact defect as fixed, in the other copy.
An unparseable well label yields `well_token=None`, which **disables** the per-well filter in the loose-file fallback, so every well's images are accepted into that one well.
An Overlay cell can never carry the `raw` uncorrected badge, so the status line counts uncorrected cells no badge ever identifies.
`lut_by_channel` / `tint_by_channel` are neither persisted nor cleared on swap: a bright plate's LUT renders the next plate black.
A ratio cell's raw-fallback is recorded under the numerator/denominator channel, so it is never badged and is counted under a channel absent from the grid.
`composite_column_rgb` calls `_row_display_opts(ctx, r)` with no channel, so it always loads the **raw** frame for a corrected channel. Dead today (re-export only).
`_parse_lut`'s no-spec fallback applies column 0's channel LUT to the whole row. Reachable only with an empty `channel_opts`.
Overlay cells install a hover readout keyed on the sentinel channel, so their pixel readout can never resolve and is always empty.
Two filename classifiers; the one the scan path uses has no `_phase` entry, so a `Role.PHASE` output would be served as a raw fluor frame. Docs name `image_identity` the single source of truth.

`merge_sample_definitions` reads only the **legacy v1** `rep_sets`/`groups`; today's on-disk shape is v2 `selections`. Its result *replaces* dataset 1's whole block. Reproduced: merging two plates with current-app Sample Definitions yields `{"well_labels": {...}, "rep_sets": [], "groups": []}` — every selection, replicate set, group, plot group, `current_id` and `notes` from **both** datasets gone, reported as a clean success. Concatenate preserves what Merge Plates deletes.

No run-time destination check: `destination_problem` / `resume_state(...).mismatched` are consulted only by `view.py`. A queued OME job overwrites each `in/<WELL>.zip` while `out/` survives — measurements that no longer match their inputs, reported as success; and a `mismatched` marker is ignored, stitching one folder from two mappings.

`apply_repairs` rewrites the live `out/pipeline_info.json` with a truncating `write_text`, while its sibling `validate/record.py:152` writes the same file tmp + `Path.replace`. A crash mid-apply destroys `cell_gating`, `sample_definitions`, `ratios` and `notes` — the four blocks this module's docstring is a paragraph about preserving — with no backup.

`_remap._rename` discards `rewrite_member_field`'s `was_rewritten` flag, so a member failing the structural gate keeps dataset 2's original well token inside the destination well's archive, silently. The CSV row is equally unrewritten, so the `dest_in_names` check still passes.

In-place mode zips and unlinks the TIFs of **every** well-named subfolder under the source, including pre-existing ones; the preview is non-recursive and loose-TIF-only. Bytes survive in the archives, so this is unannounced scope rather than loss — but preview ≠ apply on the pane's one destructive path.

`row_matches` reads the `timepoint_hours` **column** and `member_matches` reads the **filename** token. A legacy CSV with a blank `timepoint_hours` loses every row while all images copy, and `_verify` names the wrong cause.

Two containers canonicalising to the same well (`A1.zip` + `A01.zip`) collapse by plain dict overwrite in glob order. The `out_csvs` sibling documents its identical overwrite and names the caller that must not trust it; the input side has no warning and every copy tool trusts it.

The tier-1 whole-file path writes with `shutil.copy2` straight onto `dest`, outside the `atomic_zip` guarantee the module docstring states without exception. An interrupted wells-only Subset leaves a truncated `in/<WELL>.zip`.

`atomic_zip`'s verification is name-only. With 200 bytes flipped in the deflate stream the archive still publishes; `testzip()` reports `Bad CRC-32`. The invariant verified is "the index is complete", not the docstring's "readable".

`replace_folder_with_archive`'s `resolve()` identity conflates symlink and hardlink aliases in both directions: an archived symlink is reported as `kept`, and a second name for an archived file is destroyed by the folder removal though the archive holds no member under that name.
`copy2`/`move` silently overwrite same-basename files under `--recursive`; the progress line counts sources, not survivors.
`_launch` returns silently on an empty source or destination with no `jobFinished`, so a queued job is marked `running` and the queue bridge stalls forever.
The `seg_fp` restamp is set only inside `with swallow(...)`; on a failed stat the entry silently keeps the **source** dataset's fingerprint and the carried-over override is later discarded as stale.

The 500 ms debounce has no flush-all; `closeEvent` force-saves only `view_state`. An edit to ratios, heatmap layouts, cell overrides, line order, plot groups, notes, sample definitions, QC params or crop region made within 500 ms of ⌘W is lost, and a pending timer surviving `begin_load` writes into the **next** dataset's files.
`ExportPrefsState.axis_prefs` (per-figure x/y limits, log flags, mark styling) survives a dataset swap; `apply_export_style_prefs` re-applies plate A's `y_lim_max` to plate B on every redraw.

`except OSError: pass` plus an absent `<well>_out.zip` makes the v2 staleness fingerprint fail open, and the compensating warning is gated on `file_version < 2`, so a v2 file warns about nothing.

`VIEW_DOMAINS` claims `line_order` but `reset_view` never saves it, so the stale order returns on the next load and permanently reorders `selections`. The module's own promise is "what resets live must equal what is dropped from disk".

`absent_wells` / `absent_solo` survive a dataset swap and are reassigned only inside `restore()`, which is skipped when the new dataset has no `view_state` section: dataset A's wells get unioned into B's saved selection.
The heatmap timepoint is persisted as a combo **index**, which §9.7's add-timepoints workflow invalidates.
`well_labels` are hydrated pruned to loaded wells and then autosaved back, erasing labels for wells absent from a subset load. `view_state` solved this with `absent_wells`; this path did not.
Unlocked read-modify-write of `pipeline_info.json` from a viewer sharing a window with a running Analyze pass; a lost update reverts `available_timepoints` / `fluor_tokens` — the §12.3 symptom.
A bare mid-function `return` skips `apply_range` and the whole gating-hydration tail, so `threshold_min/max` keep the previous dataset's range (`begin_load` clears only the cache).
An aborted run's `_after_csv` stamps the old threshold into the **new** dataset's `pipeline_info.json`.
A plate edit rewrites a group's membership from the plate alone, permanently dropping wells the current dataset does not hold — and autosaves that.
A `schema_version` mismatch logs "applying defaults" and then uses the doc unchanged: no migration, no discard (contrast `view_state._migrate`).
`_confirm_clear` falls through to clearing when the confirmation dialog raises — an unconfirmed destructive wipe of the gallery and its PNGs.

The comma group `#RailNavRow:hover QLabel, #RailNavRow[active="true"] QLabel {color: text_primary}` bakes `text_primary` into **every** row label's palette, killing the base `text_secondary` rule. Isolated repro: the `[active]` rule alone gives `[(False,'#98a2b3'),(True,'#e6e9ef')]`; adding the `:hover` sibling to the same group gives `[(True…),(True…)]`. Review's left rail draws every section at full strength and the selected one is not distinguished.

`_Segment.paintEvent` blanks `opt.text` and draws from the palette; `QStyleSheetStyle` fills only the enabled/disabled colour *groups*, never `:checked`/`:hover`, so those QSS rules are dead. Measured: brightest checked pixel `#969ca9` vs unchecked `#98a2b3`, where `text_primary` is `#E6E9EF`. Only the fill differs.

`_reposition_hint` gates on `isVisible()`, which is False while any ancestor is hidden — exactly during build and while a popover is closed. Measured on the real `LutSelector`: the "32 / 32" chip opens at `QRect(0,0,56,15)` with right margin 0, corrects to `QRect(202,7,49,15)` only after typing, and regresses on every re-open. `isVisibleTo(self)` is the predicate needed.

The glyph is rendered at a hardcoded `15` logical px inside a font-derived box (`max(12, fontMetrics().height())`). It is 15×15 in a 14×14 box today, and at 150 % font the box grows and the ink does not — the sweep converted the reservation, not the ink.

`set_well_enabled(w, False)` drops the well from `_selected` but emits no `selectionChanged`, while its sibling `set_enabled_wells` explicitly does. The plate silently desynchronises from the app-wide `_selected_wells`.

The `_GREY` theme overrides `accent`, `accent_hover`, `accent_pressed`, `accent_dim` and `accent_fg` but **not** `accent2`. ARCHITECTURE §7/§8 require `accent2` to read as a neighbour of `accent`; under `grey` the hue gap goes 38° → 55° with diverging saturation, so the pair stops reading as one family on every remote-run plate.
`text_disabled = "#A0AEC0"` is *brighter* than `text_secondary` `#98A2B3` while claiming the disabled-label role; all seven `:disabled` rules in `qss()` use `text_faint` instead.

`#Stepper QLineEdit#StepperEdit {color: text_primary}` has no `:disabled` variant and its two-ID specificity beats the app sheet's `QLineEdit:disabled`. Latent — none of the 14 construction sites disables one.
`setThemeToggleVisible(False)` hides `_preview_chip`, but `_sync_theme_ui` re-shows it on the next `setPlotTheme`. Latent — no caller uses the API.

Raw `QColor(0,0,0,α)` where `drawer.py:58` uses `with_alpha(theme.Colors.ink_dark, 0.35)` and `popover.py:79` uses the token — four spellings of one shadow across four sibling overlays, two of which cannot follow a theme.

`font-size: 10px` in QSS and bare margin/spacing literals in the two modules whose header comments cite §8 for their *named* width constants. Invisible to `test_hardcoded_tokens.py`, which scans only `setFixed*`/`setMinimum*`/`setMaximum*` arguments.
Violin's `spec.missing` skips the violin but the raw fraction dot was already appended and still draws.
`MaxNLocator(integer=False)` contradicts the comment directly above it.
Colour-by-time hardcodes `markersize=6`, ignoring the `marker_size` preference.
A hover miss clears the status line on every mouse move, erasing fold-change shortfall warnings.

A bare `<date>` in the manual is parsed by `QTextDocument.setMarkdown` as an unclosed HTML tag, and everything after it is dropped from the render. Repro: `'Para one.

reads *checked <date>* …

After paragraph two.
'` → `'Para one.
reads checked 
'`. On the real manual every block after line 991 renders empty, so `_render_manual_html` injects 27 anchors for 85 headings and **29 of the 41 `help_topics` targets have none** — help opened from Bar Plots, Cell Gating, Job Queue, Merge Plates and 25 other pages leaves the drawer at the top of a manual that also stops at "Home". `tests/test_help_topics.py` matches topics against markdown headings, never against the render, so it cannot see this. A second bare `<date>` sits at line 3097.

`domain/` transitively imports PySide6 via `core.channel_state_controller → core.ui_helpers → PySide6.QtCore`. `tests/test_qt_free_layers.py` walks direct imports inside the listed roots only, so a one-hop detour through `core/` is invisible to it while docstrings cite that test as the guarantee. Observed as `ImportError: libQt6Core.so.6` on a bare `import well_viewer.domain.fold_change`.

`F821` is disabled globally, which is the blind spot CLAUDE.md §7.5 #11 records. All 45 current hits are annotation-only under `from __future__ import annotations` (harmless at runtime, fatal to `typing.get_type_hints`), including `pipeline/io.py:454` where `io` is never imported.

Seven broad `except Exception: pass` handlers. Both files sit outside `test_no_silent_except.py`'s roots, so the rule CLAUDE.md states as "no silent `except Exception: pass` anywhere" is unenforced there. Defensible in pre-logging startup code; the coverage gap is the finding.
`redraw_requested` has no emitter and no subscriber, while ARCHITECTURE §5.9 claims every bus signal is load-bearing and `test_architecture_contracts.py:449` freezes the dead signal in place.
`_FEATURE_STATE_OWNERS` omits `heatmap`, `scatter`, `distribution`, `smfish` and `home`, so those five give a bare `AttributeError` instead of the documented "feature disabled" message.
Two flags ship `True`; ARCHITECTURE §10.2 says "off by default", names a flag (`REVIEW_IMAGE_CHSW_DEBUG`) that does not exist, and `allwell.py:1686` wires only 4 of 9.
`figure_pref_key(ctx, None)` matches the first *unregistered* slot (`None is None`), returns a wrong key and skips its own anti-silence warning; `redraw_app:177` can pass `None`.
`has_plottable_selection`'s docstring claims four callers it does not have; the divergence it papers over is the lineplot `well_paths` filter above.
§12.4 points at `preview/controller.classify_member`; the implementation is in `well_viewer/data/zip_members.py`, and that module is a re-export shim.
The Home section states both `role="editor"` and `role="picker"` for the same plate; the code uses `"editor"`.

`from_block`'s docstring says it returns 4 values; it returns 5, so a caller unpacking the documented shape raises `ValueError`.
States ARCHITECTURE.md is "~2600 lines"; it is 8,171.
The exhausted-budget `OSError(str)` carries `errno=None` and says "write" for read call sites; `cleanup` is skipped for non-`OSError` failures, contradicting "after every failed attempt".
Two docstrings state atomicity/readability guarantees the code does not provide (see Theme 5).
